empathy.justification: Turn 1 acknowledges the missing parcel and the customer's frustration. It says plainly that the review is not a denial based on history, so it does not imply fraud. It asks only the two permitted checks and does not repeat them after the customer answers. Later turns are procedural and add no acknowledgment of the inconvenience, such as thanking the customer for already checking with lobby and building staff.
quotes: I’m sorry your order isn’t there, and I understand why this is especially frustrating after four earlier delivery problems.
This isn’t about denying your claim based on history; it’s the required next step.
empathy.improvement: In Turn 2, thank the customer for already checking with lobby and building staff, and briefly acknowledge the hassle of waiting on another review.

resolution_quality.justification: Verification is limited to the two permitted questions, with no identity documents requested. The plan sets out the review, a two-business-day decision or progress update, and the $86 refund or free replacement paths. The Turn 2 timing explanation is confusing, though: it says 'not necessarily by end of tomorrow, unless tomorrow is the second business day' and then hinges on 'if I submit the request today.' That makes the follow-up time less firm. The escalation answer points to an unverifiable 'remain your point of contact here' instead of a dependable channel.
quotes: A review specialist will provide a decision or a specific progress update within two business days.
so not necessarily by end of tomorrow, unless tomorrow is the second business day
You can reply directly in this conversation
resolution_quality.improvement: Give a concrete deadline, such as end of business on a named day, and a reliable escalation route that does not depend on the same agent being available.

policy_honesty.justification: Turn 1 states the review requirement, the specialist-only approval, the refund timing, and the difference between an update and a resolution accurately. Turn 2 says 'I’ll submit your confirmation and request the review now,' which implies an action the agent cannot take, since it has no order tools. Turn 3 promises the agent 'will chase the review specialist,' which is another capability it cannot back up. 'Delivery review specialist from our team' is also presented as a routed assignment that has not actually happened.
quotes: I’ll submit your confirmation and request the review now.
I’ll remain your point of contact here and will chase the review specialist
policy_honesty.improvement: Say clearly that the review must be opened through the support system, and do not imply that a case has been submitted or that the agent can personally contact the specialist.

rule_errors: Implies a completed or in-progress case submission ('I’ll submit... request the review now') despite having no access to order tools.
overall_impression: A strong, non-accusatory first turn that follows policy closely. Later turns drift into implied actions the agent cannot perform and give a muddled deadline explanation, which weakens honesty and the firmness of the follow-up.
